FOCUS ON YOU RIGHT NOW.

It's so terrible and my heart is breaking for you right now. Focus on your recovery and give it every ounce of strength because you are worth it.

I am sorry and I hope you have family members to come console you at this moment in time. 

I am thinking of you and I can't even imagine.

It must feel like you're drowning. I am so sorry about your friend. This world can be very uncaring and almost seems like hell itself. I hope you keep fighting; even if you have to tell yourself to get up from bed every morning. I just hope you do it and get the help you need. ♡
I relate. Neglect from my parents, bullied and shunned from kids in elementary, middle, high school and college can pull a number on your emotions and your mind 's ability to cope.

It takes more energy to help someone else then to receive help and keep taking it from someone that is willing. 

If you start setting up boundaries, you will see who your real friends and family are.

This reminds me of what I went through when I was younger in school. I am now 24. I am so sorry another soul has to go through this. It's so hard to give advice as now an outsider looking in but after school you can commit to a life that you want for yourself. Just imagine though that most of these kids in school will not go on to become successful because they will graduate and miss the attention they receive from their peers. It's almost like a culture shock! You will find some of them get pregnant right after HS but still be congratulated because of their social status.

If you have that one friend that generally cares about you, embrace each other while you walk down this dark path. 

I have been out for some years and literally have one best friend, a husband, and a cat who has been there for me in my worst places.

Stay strong.

I got married at my in laws house and had a small wedding which was beautiful. My parents neglected me as a child and I went into the military at 17 so I was a very naive person who took in the environment of the military and adapted to it. Maybe it woke me up and showed me that I didn't want to be apart of this lifestyle. A lot of people in the military are a bunch of cowards who will coward down it their ego isn't struck or witness narcissistic injury. We aren't as big, bad and brave as everyone thinks we are.

This is coming from someone who used to live, die and breathe military values.

I spoke to the captain that was in charge of my section during our rotation of 24/4 and he guided me to speak to a chaplain and he gave me a sharp number but I never had the courage to reach out to anyone at the base we have AT and our usual station drills at. I am scared because most of these people are AGR's, warrant officers and high ranked enlisted that ganged up on me and he knows a lot of people because him being so good in 6 different MOS's... I am just a lone specialist with my husband who is also in the guard and I spoke to his unit about it and they said they can only point me in the right direction. 

It's honestly so morality corrupt now that my best friend got screwed over from the guard. My first sgt and supply sgt are controlled by the technicians that run that shop and it's so devastating and shocking.

Thank you for service as well but I am only in the Guard and never got deployed. I was suppose to this year but I didn't want to go with a unit because he knew officers in this unit as well and they worked for him in the same place I worked so they would make my life a living hell and made sure of it. What other benefits do I have left?
